newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: At least 100 hurt in Manila's New Year revelry.
newsitem.headline: At least 100 hurt in Manila's New Year revelry.

text.p: At least 100 people, including a five-year-old child, were hurt by stray bullets and firecracker blasts during New Year celebrations in Manila, government and hospital officials said on Wednesday.

The number of injured, taken from the 10 biggest hospitals in Manila, was significantly lower than last year, said Health Secretary Carmencita Reodica, who led a campaign against the use of locally-made firecrackers to mark the New Year.
"The campaign has been successful...Our biggest hospitals have reported a 50 to 60 percent reduction in the number of cases this year," Reodica said.
Last year, 13 people died and more than 800 were injured by firecracker blasts.
Filipinos believe loud blasts drive away bad luck and evil spirits that hounded them in the past year. Some gun owners fired their guns into the air to welcome the new year.
Many of the victims from the celebrations were teenagers, Reodica said.
Most suffered burns, while a few had to have limbs amputated. Four of those admitted to hospitals were hit by stray bullets.

The Disaster Management Unit of the Department of Health said the most serious case was a five-year old child who suffered cerebral contusion, or bruising of the brain, from a stray firecracker in Manila.

In northern Baguio city, a row of stalls selling firecrackers burned down after a firecracker hit one of the stalls. City secretary Jose Taguba said a 13-year-old boy was hurt in the ensuing stampede.
